title: Pesapallo
summary: A fast Finnish bat-and-ball sport on a summer field. The ball is tossed straight up over the plate, the batter strikes it into the fair field and runs a zigzag course of four bases, and the further the ball travels, the further the run can go.
howToPlay: Press beside the batter and pull back: the dotted line shows the direction of the hit and how hard you will strike.
Release to swing. Aim for open grass between the fielders' reach, in the fair field.
Six hits make a round. A ball that lands past the first base zone scores a run, and each base further is worth more, up to the home run zone.
rules: The ball must land inside the field to count. A ball that leaves the sides or the far end scores nothing.
A ball that lands in the first zone scores 1, in the second 2, in the third 3 and in the home run zone 4.
A ball that lands short of the first base zone scores nothing.
All six hits count when the round ends.
Watch and learn plays a round for you with the best hit it can find.
heritageNote: Pesäpallo was shaped in Finland in the 1920s by Lauri Pihkala, who joined older Finnish ball-batting games with ideas from North American baseball. It is often called Finland's national sport and was shown at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics; clubs and leagues keep it alive across the country each summer.
